status: DRAFT v0.1: not yet reviewed, pretested or calibrated.
notes: High pole is consistently 'more traditional definitions / fewer protections'. Uses 'sex at birth' and 'gender identity' as descriptive terms, each defined.

items.stem: What should the law be on same-sex couples getting married?
items.scope: Civil marriage under the law, not religious ceremonies.
items.context: Same-sex marriage has been legal nationwide since 2015.
options: Legal marriage in every state, as today
Civil unions with the same legal rights, but not called marriage
Each state should decide
No legal recognition

facts.claim: Obergefell v. Hodges (2015); Respect for Marriage Act (2022) requires recognition of marriages from other states

items.stem: Should same-sex couples be able to adopt children on the same terms as other couples?
items.scope: Adoption and foster care through state-funded agencies.
options: Yes, through every agency
Yes, but religious agencies can decline to place children with them
No

items.stem: Should a business be allowed to refuse to serve a same-sex wedding because of the owner's religious beliefs?
items.scope: Businesses like bakeries, florists and photographers. Other cases come next.
options: No; it must serve all customers equally
Only businesses creating custom expressive work, like a designed cake or photographs
Yes, any business

items.stem: Should each of these be allowed to refuse because of their religious beliefs?
options: Should not be allowed to refuse
Should be allowed to refuse

cases.text: A landlord refusing to rent an apartment to a same-sex couple
A pharmacist refusing to fill a prescription for birth control
A counselor refusing to help a client with a gender transition

items.stem: What should the law be on medical treatments for minors who identify as transgender?
items.scope: Treatments like puberty blockers, hormones and surgery for people under 18. Specific treatments come next.
items.context: About half the states ban these treatments for minors. The Supreme Court upheld such a ban in 2025.
options: Allowed when the young person, parents and doctors agree
Allowed only after extended evaluation by specialists, and no surgery before 18
Banned under 18, except in research studies
Banned under 18

facts.claim: United States v. Skrmetti (June 2025) upheld Tennessee's ban; about 27 states restrict gender-transition care for minors
facts.source: 605 U.S. ___ (2025); KFF / Movement Advancement Project tracking

definitions.text: Medicines that pause the physical changes of puberty while they are taken.

items.stem: For a 16-year-old who identifies as transgender, with parental consent, should each of these be allowed?
options: Allowed
Not allowed

cases.text: Using a new name and dressing as the other gender, with no medical treatment
Hormones of the other sex (testosterone or estrogen)

items.stem: In college and professional sports, should transgender women compete in women's events?
items.scope: Competitive events with titles, records or prize money.
options: Yes
Yes, if they meet hormone-level rules
Only if they did not go through male puberty
No; they should compete in men's or open categories

definitions.text: People who were identified as male at birth and identify as women.

items.stem: Which public restrooms and locker rooms should transgender people use?
items.scope: Shared facilities in schools and government buildings.
options: Those matching their gender identity
Those matching their gender identity, with private single-person options available to anyone
Private single-person facilities, or those matching their sex at birth
Only those matching their sex at birth

definitions.text: A person's inner sense of being a man, a woman, or something else, which may differ from the sex recorded at birth.

items.stem: What should the sex shown on passports and driver's licenses be based on?
options: Gender identity, including an "X" option
Gender identity, male or female only
Sex at birth, but changes allowed after medical transition
Sex at birth only

items.stem: Should teachers use a student's chosen name and pronouns when they don't match the student's sex at birth?
options: Yes, whenever the student asks
Yes, but only with a parent's consent
No; use names and pronouns matching sex at birth

items.stem: If a student tells school staff they identify as a different gender, should the school tell the student's parents?
options: Only if the student agrees
Yes, unless staff believe the student would be at risk of abuse
Yes, always

items.stem: Should federal law ban discrimination against gay and transgender people in housing, public services and businesses open to the public?
items.scope: Employment is already covered under a 2020 Supreme Court ruling. Exemptions come next.
options: Yes, for both sexual orientation and gender identity
Yes, for sexual orientation, but not gender identity
No federal law; leave it to states
No such protections at any level

facts.claim: Bostock v. Clayton County (2020): Title VII employment protections cover sexual orientation and gender identity

items.stem: Under such a law, should each of these be exempt?
options: Should not be exempt
Should be exempt

cases.text: Churches, when hiring staff who don't lead worship
Religious schools, for admissions and hiring
Owners renting out a room in their own home
